description: Probes what is verifiable on disk about AAS security: where security lives in the spec series, the V3.0 removal of security from the AAS metamodel and of PDP/PEP/PIP and certificates from the information model, the AASd- to AASs- renaming and security constraints (Part 1 v3.0 annex tables), and the Batteries Regulation Art. 77(2) access categories. IDTA-01004 Part 4 itself (Access Rule Model) is NOT on disk and is not probed.

items.question: Which part of the AAS specification series covers the security metamodel (access control)?
items.expected_answer: Part 4 (IDTA-01004). Part 1 covers the core metamodel, Part 5 the AASX format and the Part 3 series the data specifications.

items.question: Does an AssetAdministrationShell in metamodel V3.0 still carry a 'security' attribute that points at its access control?
items.expected_answer: No. V3.0 removed the security attribute from the Asset Administration Shell; security is now its own part, and the AAS and its elements are referenced from Security rather than the AAS referencing it.

citation.document: IDTA-01001 Part 1 Metamodel (Annex H: Metamodel Changes V3.0 vs. V2.0.1)
citation.section: Annex H, Changes V3.0 vs. V2.0.1, major changes
citation.quote: REMOVED: Security attribute removed from Asset Administration Shell, Access Control remains part of the specification

items.question: Are policy decision points, policy enforcement points and policy information points part of the V3.0 AAS information model?
items.expected_answer: No. They were removed: they are not part of the information model but of the server infrastructure hosting the Asset Administration Shells.

citation.document: IDTA-01001 Part 1 Metamodel (Annex: Metamodel Changes V3.0RC02 vs. V2.0.1 - Security Part)
citation.section: Metamodel Changes V3.0RC02 vs. V2.0.1 - Security Part, changes
citation.quote: policy decision point, policy enforcement point, and policy information points are not part of information model but of server infrastructure hosting the Asset Administration Shells

items.question: Does the V3 AAS security metamodel still model certificates (Certificate / BlobCertificate) for X.509 trust anchors?
items.expected_answer: No. Certificate handling was removed from the information model (Certificate, BlobCertificate and Security/certificate removed); it belongs to the server infrastructure hosting the AAS.

citation.document: IDTA-01001 Part 1 Metamodel (Annex: Metamodel Changes V3.0RC02 vs. V2.0.1 - Security Part)
citation.section: Metamodel Changes V3.0RC02 vs. V2.0.1 - Security Part, changes
citation.quote: Removed: Certificate Handling not part of information model but of server infrastructure hosting the Asset Administration Shells

items.question: A V3.0 validator reports AASd-010 and AASd-011 on permission properties. Are those still Part 1 metamodel constraint ids?
items.expected_answer: No. Security-part constraints were renamed from the AASd- pattern to AASs- (AASd-010 became AASs-010, AASd-011 became AASs-011); they belong to the security part, not Part 1.

citation.document: IDTA-01001 Part 1 Metamodel (Annex: Metamodel Changes V3.0RC01 - Security Part)
citation.section: Metamodel Changes V3.0RC01 - Security Part, major changes; Table 40
citation.quote: Constraints for security part renamed from pattern AASd- to AASs-.

items.question: Under constraint AASs-010, which category must the property referenced in Permission/permission have?

citation.document: IDTA-01001 Part 1 Metamodel (Annex: Table 27 New, Changed or Removed Constraints Security)
citation.quote: Constraint AASs-010: the property referenced in Permission/permission shall have the category "CONSTANT".

items.question: Why was constraint AASs-009 (external policy administration point or own access control) dropped in V3.0RC02?
items.expected_answer: It was removed because the class PolicyAdministrationPoint was removed.

citation.document: IDTA-01001 Part 1 Metamodel (Annex: Table 27 New, Changed or Removed Constraints Security)
citation.quote: AASs-009 Removed Removed since class PolicyAdministrationPoint was removed

items.question: In the V3.0 security metamodel, does AccessPermissionRule still inherit from Referable and Qualifiable?
items.expected_answer: No. AccessPermissionRule no longer inherits from Referable nor from Qualifiable; a constraint attribute substitutes for the inherited qualifiers.

citation.document: IDTA-01001 Part 1 Metamodel (Annex: Table 25 Changes w.r.t. Security)
citation.quote: AccessPermissionRule No longer inherits from Referable No longer inherits from Qualifiable

items.question: Can a Qualifiable element in V3.0 carry a Formula (as qualifiers could in V2)?
items.expected_answer: No. Formula is now an abstract class used only in the security part, no longer in Qualifiables (and Formula/dependsOn was removed).

citation.document: IDTA-01001 Part 1 Metamodel (Annex: Table 25 Changes w.r.t. Security)
citation.quote: Formula Now abstract class, only used in security part (no longer used in Qualifiables)

items.question: How are the PermissionKind enumeration literals spelled since V2.0 (e.g. 'not applicable')?
items.expected_answer: With a capital first letter and no space: Allow, Deny, NotApplicable, Undefined.

citation.document: IDTA-01001 Part 1 Metamodel (Annex: Table 46 Changes Metamodel w.r.t. V1.0 Security)
citation.quote: Now PermissionKind/NotApplicable starts with capital letter for enumeration values

items.question: Under the EU Batteries Regulation 2023/1542 Art. 77(2), who may access the battery passport information of Annex XIII point 3?
items.expected_answer: Only notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission (information under points 2 and 3 of Annex XIII).

citation.quote: (b) information accessible only to notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission in accordance with points 2 and 3 of Annex XIII

items.question: Under Batteries Regulation Art. 77(2), which Annex XIII points are accessible to persons with a legitimate interest?
items.expected_answer: Points 2 and 4 of Annex XIII (point 1 is public; points 2 and 3 go to notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission).

citation.quote: legitimate interest in accessing and processing that information for the purposes referred to in points (a) and (b) of the third subparagraph in accordance with points 2 and 4 of Annex XIII

items.question: Does the Batteries Regulation itself enumerate which persons count as having a 'legitimate interest' for battery passport access?
items.expected_answer: No. Article 77(9) requires the Commission to adopt implementing acts by 18 August 2026 specifying which persons are to be considered persons with a legitimate interest and what they may access.

citation.quote: By 18 August 2026, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts specifying which persons are to be considered persons with a legitimate interest

items.question: Does IDTA-01004 Part 4 say anything about the format of access tokens?
items.expected_answer: Yes. AAS Security uses signed JWT (JSON Web Token) bearer tokens as access tokens, as defined in RFC 7519; the authentication flow that produces them is left open (OAuth 2.0 or OIDC can be used).

citation.document: IDTA-01004 Part 4 Security (official PDF, paged text)
citation.quote: AAS Security uses signed JWT (JSON Web Token) bearer tokens as Access Tokens, as they are defined in RFC 7519.

items.question: Does IDTA-01004 Part 4 v3.1 define a digital signature format for AAS content?
items.expected_answer: No. Part 4 v3.1 does not specify a native, data-bound protection mechanism such as digital signatures; it points to the /$signed endpoint of the API specification IDTA-01002 (plain JWS).

citation.document: IDTA-01004 Part 4 Security (official PDF, paged text)
citation.quote: This document does not specify a native way to protect AAS elements with data-bound protection mechanisms such as digital signatures.
citation.section: Accountability for AAS Content and Digital Signatures
